land.text: Lavo had been 'one of the supra-regional centres of the Dvaravati mandalas'; Kalavarnadisharaja 'succeeded at Nakhon Pathom in 641' and in 648 'transferred the political centre to the newly founded settlement'

predecessors.note: Dvaravati has no Cliopatria row and no dossier yet. The page calls it a cultural sphere rather than a centralised state, so Cliopatria's 638-647 Lavo shape is Dvaravati's land.

land.text: 'Lavo was annexed into Ayutthaya in 1388'; Ramesuan retook Ayutthaya from Thong Lan in 1388, bringing 'Ayutthaya and Lavo under one ruler'

successors.note: Cliopatria keeps a Lavo shape to 1394.

capitals.name: Lopburi (Lavapura)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Lopburi (Lavapura) before the 1080s'. The page's table is garbled and assigns some rulers to Lavapura and some to Ayodhya.

capitals.name: Ayodhya (Xian)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Ayodhya as capital (Xian): 1082-1351'; Narai I 'moved the capital to Ayodhya in the 1080s'. The page gives Lavapura seats in the same years (Chaliang 1106-1181, Angkor 1181-1218, Phraek Si Racha 1218-1351), so the dot is the page's infobox reading, not settled. Coordinates are Ayutthaya's (researcher's).

capitals.name: Lopburi (Lavapura)
capitals.note: Ayutthaya page: 'King Uthong had his son, Prince Ramesuan, the ruler of Lopburi'; the Lavo page: after losing Ayutthaya in 1370 Ramesuan 'retreated to Lavo'.

correction.text: The same outline, but Dvaravati's land for 638-647 (years only)

keyframe_review.note: Years 638-647 are before Lavo: infobox 'Establishment: 648'; Kalavarnadisharaja 'reduced Tou Yuan to vassal status in 647' and in 648 founded the new settlement. The Chao Phraya outline (127,642 km2) is the Dvaravati sphere's land for those years, to be drawn from a Dvaravati dossier. The page also reports a foundation 'a century earlier, in 538' and a settlement possibly begun in 629.

correction.text: The same outline, drawn from 648 to 660 (years only)

keyframe_review.note: Years only: 648-660. Infobox 'Establishment: 648'. The 127,761 km2 outline compares with the infobox 'approximately 170,000 km2' (no year given): ratio 0.75, within the factor of two.

126,307 km2 against the infobox's 170,000 km2 (undated): ratio 0.74. The page gives no boundary; the lower Chao Phraya basin from Lopburi is the 'lower Chao Phraya basin' of the lead. Around the late seventh century 'Lavo expanded north' (Camadevi legend), which the page does not date or map.

The page is silent on any border move in 718-805. Balipatijaya 'took Lavo about 700', but the page does not say whose ruler he was or what land changed hands; the shape stands. 126,451 km2, ratio 0.74 to the infobox figure.

correction.text: The same outline, ended in 927 (years only)

keyframe_review.note: Years only: 806-927. The realm's outline for 806-1002 stands (126,430 km2, ratio 0.74 to the infobox's undated 170,000 km2), but Tambralinga held Lavo from 928 to 946 ('Tambralinga vassal: 927-946'), so the shape is interrupted; the page also records battles with Haripunjaya 925-927.

New keyframe 946-1002: the same outline back under its own rule after the Tambralinga years (infobox 'Tambralinga vassal: 927-946'; the table has Kampoch, 930-946?, 'As a tributary state of Tambralinga'). Angkor's overlordship ('Angkor vassal: 946-1052' in the infobox) is the Khmer dossier's to show as a tint; Lavo 'was devastated from the east in 946 and 1001'.

correction.text: The same outline, ended in 1005 (years only); Khmer-governed from 1006 to 1051

keyframe_review.note: Years only: 1003-1005. The page dates Angkor's destruction of Lavo to 1001 (infobox), 'around 1005' (table) and Lakshmipativarman's governorship to 1006, with a reading placing the conquest 'between 1011 and 1014'; from 1006 Lavo was 'governed by a Cambodian prince, as part of Angkor's vassal state'. Cliopatria's Khmer shape takes the ground in 1028; the ledger records Angkor's loss event in 1006.

correction.text: The 1056 outline (Chao Phraya basin and the isthmus) under Chandrachota

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1052-1055: Lavo returns to a ruler of its own. Infobox 'Reclaimed by Suphannabhum/Haripunjaya: 1052'; 'Haripunjaya's Thamikaraj, with Suphannabhum's help, took Lavo' in 1052 and Chandrachota reigned 1052-1069 (the Haripunjaya page: Adityaraja 'annexed Lavo in 1052 and appointed his brother, Chadachota, the king of Lavo'). The 1056 outline is used because the page gives no extent for these four years; Cliopatria draws Khmer land here.

143,092 km2 against the infobox's 170,000 km2: ratio 0.84. The shape reaches south to 10.1 N (the isthmus at Chumphon); that southern bulge (about 50 cells) lies inside Cliopatria's Khmer shape of 1028, so it comes with the 1052 gain from Angkor, but no page opened names a southern conquest (Tambralinga's hold on Lavo ended in 946). Left as drawn, flagged unverified.

correction.text: The same outline, ended in 1180 (years only)

keyframe_review.note: Years only: 1066-1180. 'Jayavarman VII appointed Narupatidnavarman to govern Lavapura in 1181' (table 'Angkor 1181-1218'), so Lavo is Angkor's from 1181, not 1188 as Cliopatria's Khmer shape begins. In between the page gives Lavo's own line: Narai I (1082-1087), Phra Chao Luang (1089-1111), a Song mission in 1115, 'Lavo gained independence: 1155'; the 1106 change of dynasty (Kesariraja of Si Satchanalai, or Phrom of Yonok) is a rename in the ledger. The 1066 outline (140,788 km2) differs from the 1056 one only by the western edge; the page does not explain the change.

correction.text: The 1241 outline (the Lopburi-Ayutthaya-Suphan Buri core) for 1218-1240

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1218-1240. The page's Lavapura rows read 'Angkor 1181-1218; Phraek Si Racha 1218-1351', so Angkor's governorship ends in 1218; the page gives no extent, and the 1241 outline (42,717 km2, a third of the 1187 one) is used for 1218-1240, where Cliopatria draws the Khmer Empire. The Khmer Empire page says Indravarman II (1219-1243) 'lost western territories to Siamese Sukhothai'; the researcher reads the larger western lands of the 1187 outline as those lost lands, not Lavo's (339 cells, 316 of them inside Cliopatria's Sukhothai shape of 1241).

42,717 km2 against the infobox's 170,000 km2 (undated, evidently a peak): ratio 0.25. Lavo was independent: it joined a Ny Wang embassy to the Yuan in 1289 and sent one alone in 1299. The page does not describe the extent of Lavo in 1241-1351.

34,834 km2. The 7,900 km2 cut from the 1241 outline is the land round Ayodhya that became Ayutthaya's core: 'Formation of Ayutthaya: 1351' (infobox) and Uthong and Borommarachathirat I 'founded Ayutthaya' in 1351. The page does not map the cut; the ledger carries it as a reading.

31,880 km2: a further 3,000 km2 lost, all of it inside Ayutthaya's 1375 shape. No page opened dates it (the Ayutthaya page dates only the 'Lopburi and Suphanburi rivalry: 1370-1409' and Ramesuan's loss of Ayutthaya in 1370); the ledger carries it at confidence 1.

correction.text: The same outline, ended in 1388 (years only)

keyframe_review.note: Years only: 1385-1388. 'Lavo was annexed into Ayutthaya in 1388' (Lavo page); 'Lavo was not fully incorporated into Ayutthaya's political order until 1388' (Ayutthaya page). Cliopatria keeps the shape to 1394.

region.text: Lavapura and the lower Chao Phraya basin

ledger.note: 648: Kalavarnadisharaja founds Lavo. Infobox 'Establishment: 648'; he 'transferred the political centre to the newly founded settlement' after reducing Tou Yuan to vassal status in 647; 'a mandala in the lower Chao Phraya basin'. The page also has a foundation 'a century earlier, in 538' and Tang records of 'Tou-ho-lo'.

region.text: the Lavo-Haripunjaya frontier: 'Rathasatkara of Haripunjaya moved south, and the Lavo king Uchitthaka Chakkawat defended'; the page names no place

ledger.note: 925: Lavo and Haripunjaya fight. 'Battles between Lavo and Haripunjaya are recorded from 925 to 927.' The page gives no place; the frontier is drawn.

region.text: the Lavo-Haripunjaya frontier: 'Rathasatkara of Haripunjaya moved south, and the Lavo king Uchitthaka Chakkawat defended'; the page names no place

ledger.note: 927: the war with Haripunjaya ends as Lavo falls to Tambralinga. The Dvaravati page: Uchitthaka 'lost Lavapura to Sujita of Tambralinga in 927 CE' and 'took Haripunjaya and ruled there until 930'.

928: Tambralinga annexes Lavo. the page's '[...] left it open to annexation by Tambralinga from the south in 928'; King Jivaka 'occupied Lavo in 927-928 and appointed his son Kampoch'; infobox 'Tambralinga vassal: 927-946'. The page's own 927/928 split is kept in the note; the Lavo shape stays in the keyframes and this event overrides it.

946: Tambralinga's hold on Lavo ends. the infobox 'Tambralinga vassal: 927-946' and the table's 'As a tributary state of Tambralinga' (Kampoch, 930-946?); the infobox then reads 'Angkor vassal: 946-1052' and 'Fall of Ayodhyapura: 946', and Lavo 'was devastated from the east in 946 and 1001'. The page does not say who ruled Lavo in 946; the Angkor vassalage belongs to the Khmer dossier.

1006: Angkor takes Lavo under a Khmer governor. Lakshmipativarman's governorship 'is conventionally dated to 1006'; Suryavarman I's troops 'destroyed Lavo' (infobox 'Destroyed by Angkor: 1001'; a reading places the conquest 'between 1011 and 1014'); Lavo 'was governed by a Cambodian prince, as part of Angkor's vassal state' (Songsiri disputes Angkorian control). The Khmer Empire page is silent on the conquest and gives Suryavarman I as 1006-1050.

region.text: Lavo, taken back from Angkor by Haripunjaya's prince

ledger.note: 1052: Lavo returns to a ruler of its own. Infobox 'Reclaimed by Suphannabhum/Haripunjaya: 1052'; 'Haripunjaya's Thamikaraj, with Suphannabhum's help, took Lavo'; Chandrachota king 1052-1069. The Haripunjaya dossier carries the dependency on Haripunjaya.

1082: Narai I moves the capital to Ayodhya. 'Narai I moved the capital to Ayodhya in the 1080s' (infobox 'Ayodhya as capital (Xian): 1082-1351'); he reigned 1082-1087 and 'died with no heir in 1087'. The table also places him at Lopburi, with a different end.

1106: a new line takes the Lavapura seat. 'Kesariraja of Si Satchanalai took the Lavapura seat'; local chronicles say 'the Tai king Phrom of Yonok seized Lavo in 1106'. The state continues on the same land; the page's table assigns the seat to Chaliang 1106-1181.

1181: Jayavarman VII places Lavo under Angkor. 'Jayavarman VII appointed Narupatidnavarman to govern Lavapura in 1181' (table 'Angkor 1181-1218'); the Prasat Tor inscription records a defeat of a western monarch in 1189/90 or 1195/96. Cliopatria's Khmer shape starts in 1188.

1218: Angkor's governorship of Lavo ends. The table reads 'Angkor 1181-1218; Phraek Si Racha 1218-1351'; the page does not say why or how. Lavo is independent by 1289, when it joined a Ny Wang embassy to the Yuan. The garbled table is the only support; Cliopatria brings Lavo back in 1241.

region.text: the land round Ayodhya that became Ayutthaya's core

ledger.note: 1351: Ayutthaya is founded out of Lavo's land round Ayodhya. '4 March 1351 is conventionally given as the foundation of the Ayutthaya Kingdom'; Uthong V 'held Phetchaburi and Ayodhya by direct descent and acquired Suphannabhum and Lavo through marriage'. The Lavo page: 'In 1349 Xian and Lo-hu were joined' and Ayutthaya was founded in 1351. The land lost is the researcher's reading of the 1351 to 1352 change in Cliopatria's Lavo outline.

region.text: the strip Lavo loses between 1374 and 1375

ledger.note: 1375: Lavo cedes a further border strip to Ayutthaya. Page silent: the Ayutthaya page dates only the 'Lopburi and Suphanburi rivalry: 1370-1409' and Ramesuan's loss of Ayutthaya in 1370; the year and the strip (13 cells, all inside Cliopatria's Ayutthaya shape of 1375) are bridged from the Cliopatria change.

1388: Lavo is annexed into Ayutthaya. 'Lavo was annexed into Ayutthaya in 1388' (Lavo page); 'Ramesuan lost Ayutthaya to Borommarachathirat in 1370 but recovered it from Thong Lan in 1388', which brought 'Ayutthaya and Lavo under one ruler' and 'Lavo was not fully incorporated into Ayutthaya's political order until 1388' (Ayutthaya page).

wars.name: Lavo-Haripunjaya war (925-927)

zones.text: the Lavo-Haripunjaya frontier: 'Rathasatkara of Haripunjaya moved south, and the Lavo king Uchitthaka Chakkawat defended'; the page names no place

wars.outcome: 'Battles between Lavo and Haripunjaya are recorded from 925 to 927'; the Lavo king Uchitthaka Chakkawat defended against Rathasatkara of Haripunjaya. Tambralinga then annexed Lavo (928); the Dvaravati page has Uchitthaka flee north and rule Haripunjaya until 930.
wars.note: The page names no place and no territorial change.

wars.name: Tambralinga's conquest of Lavo (927-928)
wars.outcome: King Jivaka (Suchitra) 'occupied Lavo in 927-928', appointed his son Kampoch, and held it as a tributary 930-946; the page's '[...] left it open to annexation by Tambralinga from the south in 928'.

wars.name: Angkorian conquest of Lavo (1001-1014)
wars.outcome: Suryavarman I's troops destroyed Lavo after the nine-year civil war at Angkor (infobox 1001; table 'around 1005'); Lakshmipativarman governed from 1006; the K.1198 stele is dated 1014 and one reading puts the conquest 'between 1011 and 1014'.
wars.note: The Khmer Empire page is silent on this conquest.

wars.name: Haripunjaya's capture of Lavo (1052)
wars.outcome: 'Haripunjaya's Thamikaraj, with Suphannabhum's help, took Lavo' in 1052 and installed his brother Chandrachota as king (1052-1069).
wars.note: The Haripunjaya page gives the same year and the brother's name.

wars.name: Lavo's northward attacks on Haripunjaya (12th century)
wars.outcome: Lopburi, held by a Mon-Tai clan from Chaliang, 'marched north several times without success' in the twelfth century; no border moved.
wars.note: The span is the century; the page gives no years.

wars.name: Angkor's return to Lavapura under Jayavarman VII (1181-1196)
wars.outcome: A governor, Narupatidnavarman, was appointed in 1181; the Prasat Tor inscription records a defeat of a western monarch in 1189/90 or 1195/96.
wars.note: The page does not call it a war and gives no fighting for 1181 itself.

wars.name: Lopburi-Suphanburi rivalry (1370-1388)

zones.text: the Lopburi-Ayutthaya frontier of the 1370s-1380s; the page names no place

wars.outcome: Borommarachathirat I of Suphanburi took Ayutthaya from Ramesuan in 1370 ('Lopburi and Suphanburi rivalry: 1370-1409'); Ramesuan recovered it from Thong Lan in 1388, bringing 'Ayutthaya and Lavo under one ruler'; in 1408 Intharacha retook Ayutthaya for the Suphannabhum line.
wars.note: A dynastic war inside the Ayutthaya state rather than a frontier war; the zone is a reading.

certainty.note: Lavo was a mandala; no page opened gives a boundary. All frontiers (Haripunjaya to the north, the Khmer to the east, Tambralinga on the isthmus, Ayutthaya from 1351) are approximate.

sources.title: Lavo Kingdom
sources.note: Identity, 648 foundation, capitals, Tambralinga 927-946, Angkor 1001-1014 and 1181-1218, Haripunjaya 925-927 and 1052, the 1106 change, Ayutthaya 1351 and 1388, infobox area 170,000 km2 (undated). The infobox and table are garbled and conflict on several dates.

sources.title: Dvaravati
sources.note: Dvaravati as a cultural sphere (6th-11th century), not a centralised state; Lavo's rise after Tou Yuan; Uchitthaka's flight to Haripunjaya in 927.

sources.title: Khmer Empire
sources.note: Silent on Lavo's conquest by Suryavarman I (reign given as 1006-1050) and on Jayavarman VII's Lavo; Indravarman II 'lost western territories to Siamese Sukhothai'; Ayutthaya's inheritance of 'the former Khmer dependency of Lavo (Lopburi)'.

sources.title: Ayutthaya Kingdom
sources.note: 4 March 1351 founding; Ramesuan, Lopburi and the Suphanburi rivalry (1370-1409); 'Lavo was not fully incorporated into Ayutthaya's political order until 1388'. Area 400,000 km2 (undated).

sources.title: Sukhothai Kingdom
sources.note: Opened for the Sukhothai frontier of 1241-1351: Sukhothai 'drew heavily on Khmer culture by way of Lavo'; silent on Ram Khamhaeng taking Lavo or Lopburi.

sources.title: Haripuñjaya
sources.note: Adityaraja 'annexed Lavo in 1052' and installed his brother Chadachota; the Khmers 'took over Lavo from Tambralinga in 1002'.

notes: Cliopatria's single row 'Lavo Kingdom' (638-1394, twelve shapes, gaps 1028-1055 and 1188-1240 where it draws the Khmer Empire) is kept as one state: the page treats Lavo as one mandala 'from the 7th century until 1388' whose seat, dynasties and overlords change, so it is not split. Moved from Cliopatria: start 648 (not 638; 638-647 is Dvaravati's land); end 1388 (not 1394); the Khmer gaps are filled by Lavo's own keyframes where the page says Lavo had a ruler of its own (1052-1055, 1218-1240) and left to the Khmer dossier where Angkor governed it (1006-1051, 1181-1217). Not settled: the Khmer conquest date (946, 1001, c. 1005, 1006, 1011-1014 on the same page; 1006 is used, the earliest governorship); the page's garbled capital table; the southern bulge of the 1056 and 1066 shapes to 10.1 N (Khmer land in Cliopatria's 1028 shape; no page names it); the 1375 strip (conf 1); the end of Haripunjaya's hold on Lavo; the extent of Lavo in 1241-1351. The page's claim that Lavo 'gained independence' in 1155 is not drawn. Siamese chronicles claim Anawrahta of Pagan 'conquered the entire Menam valley'; the Pagan page treats it as undated chronicle claim, not drawn. Counterparts needing dossiers: dvaravati (Cliopatria lacks it; additions batch se-01-x), tambralinga (no row; southern Thailand, 928-946 and after), suphannaphum (Suphannabhum, Suphanburi, no row), plus the other se-01 parts' khmer-empire (should carry the gains of Lavo in 1006 and 1181 and the losses of 1052 and 1218, and the vassalage 946-1052) and ayutthaya-kingdom (the gains of 1351 and 1388). The Seshat pages th_lavo_k_1 and th_lavo_k_2 were not opened.
